newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended sharply lower on Thursday as they nosedived toward the end of the session, losing most of Wednesday's gains after having stayed broadly flat for most of the day.
The 10-year benchmark ended down 33 basis points at 101.91/01 at a bid yield of 5.48 percent while the long bond lost 39 basis points to close at 116.81/01 for a bid yield of 6.17 percent.
Dealers blamed the fall on stronger than expected U.S. economic data released in the afternoon, with some saying simple profit-taking was behind the correction.

Advance second-quarter U.S. gross domestic product grew at a 2.2-percent rate compared to estimates for a 1.9-percent Q2 increase. The Chicagoland Business Barometer fell to a seasonally adjusted 60.6 in July from 61.5 in June, outstripping market forecasts of 59.8.
The market was unmoved by the fact that the Dutch central bank left its key special advances rate unchanged.
Dealers said there was some demand for short paper, while one said he saw buying interest in the middle segment as market players expected the yield on long term bonds to rise in time.
Volumes remained light since market players were still looking for more clues to define the trend, dealers said.
U.S. data due on Friday include unemployment and the NAPM index for July, and June personal income and factory orders.

"In the U.S., we're seeing very low yields technically. And in the Netherlands and Germany, we're also at very low levels," one said. "We are at a historical floor, which we just can't seem to break through," he said, adding the overall picture for the bond market looked good.
"Maybe we just have to get used to these low (yield) levels," another said.
